info.title: Replay QA API
info.description:
AI-powered QA testing platform. Create projects, manage bugs, run explorations, and inspect test results.

## Continuous QA workflow

The intended loop for a coding agent keeping an app bug-free:

1. **Create a project** (`POST /projects`) for the running app — pass its `target_url` and a short `instructions` note on the key flows to focus on. Optionally include a `design_document` describing the features it should have.
2. **Let QA run.** Poll `GET /projects/{project_id}/status` until explorations and test runs finish. QA drives exploration and testing itself — do NOT start your own explorations or test runs while it is running. If you created the project with `start_exploration: false`, it stays active for session processing without initial base-site QA; use POST /projects/{project_id}/explorations when the user opts in.
3. **Read the bugs.** List open bugs (`GET /projects/{project_id}/bugs?status=open`) and fetch each one (`GET /bugs/{bug_id}`). Every bug ships with a full investigation: reproduction steps, expected vs. actual behavior, a screenshot chronology, and a root-cause analysis traced through the Replay recording (app.replay.io/recording/<id>) down to the responsible code. Verify the report against its evidence and the source before applying a fix. For GitHub issues, fetch the fix-qa-bug skill below.
4. **Mark each fix** (`PATCH /bugs/{bug_id}` with `{"status":"fixed"}`) — this automatically retries the affected journey to confirm the fix. Choose the status using the lifecycle guidance below.
open: an unresolved issue; match recurring findings to this report. fixed: a fix was applied and the issue should not recur; ignore this report during deduplication and assess any recurrence as a fresh report. invalid: the report has a problem and is discarded; keep it as a duplicate candidate so the same invalid claim is not filed again. A genuinely different defect needs its own evidence and report. wontfix: the issue is acknowledged and will recur, but new bugs should not be filed for it; match recurring findings to this report. Open, wontfix and invalid are duplicate candidates. Wontfix and invalid both suppress repeat filings; neither means a fix was applied.
5. **Loop.** After marking a bug fixed, go back to polling status and keep going until no open bugs remain.

### Resolving QA-reported GitHub issues

Fetch `GET /api/v1/skills/fix-qa-bug/SKILL.md` without credentials. Read it directly, or save it as `fix-qa-bug/SKILL.md` in your agent’s skill directory. The skill verifies evidence, closes false positives and duplicates covered by open PRs in both GitHub and QA, or creates a tested fix PR with a `Fixes <qa-bug-url>` declaration.

### GitHub App (PR and main-branch QA)

Fetch `GET /api/v1/skills/github-app/SKILL.md` without credentials: the canonical reference for installing the Replay QA GitHub App, linking a repository (`github` on `PATCH /projects/{project_id}`), every configuration parameter including the repository's `.github/replay-qa.yml` (`ignorePaths`), check results, and linking bugs to pull requests.

### Apps only reachable from your machine (reverse proxy)

If `target_url` is reachable only from your own machine (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and not the public internet, create the project with `use_reverse_proxy: true`. It then starts gated and will not run tests until you connect an outbound-only tunnel. The create response includes `reverse_proxy_setup_url`; run `replayqa proxy --project <project_id>` on a machine that can reach the app. The old copy-paste setup runbook remains available from `GET /projects/{project_id}/reverse-proxy` as an advanced fallback.

## Missing a capability?

If this API lacks something you or your agent need, contact the Replay team (see `info.contact`).

## Authentication

Bug and project endpoints require a Bearer token. The OpenAPI document and published skills are public. Which credential to use and how to get it: https://docs.replay.io/reference/api-keys

post.summary: Send a message to the project assistant. Saves the user message in the shared project chat and starts an asynchronous reply using server-loaded history. Returns turnId; poll get_project_chat_turn until done. The assistant can perform project actions requested by the message. Requires project membership; task credentials are not supported.

get.summary: Poll a project assistant reply started by your account. Returns accumulated text, events after the supplied cursor, the next cursor, status, and done. Inline UI events may require opening the project in the web app. Poll at the returned pollMs interval until done, including error or timeout.

200.description: Accumulated text, events, cursor, status, error, done, and pollMs. Use cursor as after on the next poll.

404.description: Turn not found for this account and project

post.summary: Reserve an email for a future QA project
post.description: Returns a unique receiving address without creating a project or starting QA. Pass project_email to POST /api/v1/projects using the same account. Each address can be assigned once and does not expire. Task credentials are not accepted.

get.summary: List all projects you have access to

200.description: List of projects

post.summary: Create a new QA project, optionally starting automated exploration

target_url.description: URL of the application to test

webhook_url.description: URL to receive bug report notifications. Payload: { body, referrer, callback_url, bug_id, title, severity, description, reproduction_steps, expected_behavior, actual_behavior, replay_recording_id, analysis, polish_category }

project_email.description: An unused email returned by POST /api/v1/project-emails for this account. Assigned before QA starts and used for the project inbox and default login identity. Explicit login credentials retain precedence. Omit to use the automatically derived inbox. Invalid, foreign, or already assigned emails return 400.

finished_webhook_url.description: URL to receive a notification when QA on this project finishes and has nothing left to do (no queued/running tasks or in-progress test runs, explorations, polish passes, or guidance updates). Fires once per idle transition. Payload: { event: "qa.finished", referrer, project_id, project_name, project_url, bug_count, open_bug_count, resolved_bug_count, finished_at }

backend_recording_url.description: Endpoint for creating Replay recordings of backend requests. Agents POST { requestId } to trigger, GET ?requestId=<id> to poll.

backend_log_url.description: Endpoint for fetching backend/database logs. Agents GET ?start=<ISO>&end=<ISO> to retrieve logs.

logins.description: Login credentials for the app under test

design_document.description: Markdown document describing expected app features. When provided, it is given to the app exploration as additional context for planning test journeys (the exploration still browses and records the app).

start_exploration.description: Set false to create an active project without the initial exploration or smoke-test journey/runs. Session ingestion, reviews, reports, and session-driven reproductions remain enabled. Start base-site QA later with POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/explorations. This is a creation-time option, not a project pause or a restriction on explicitly requested work.

instructions.description: Instructions for the initial AI exploration
instructions.default: Explore the app and test the main features

recording_id.description: Replay recording UUID to analyze for bugs. When provided, the project analyzes this single recording instead of exploring the target URL. target_url is not required when recording_id is set.

use_reverse_proxy.description: Set to true when target_url is only reachable from your own machine (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and not from the public internet. The project starts gated — it will not run tests until you connect a reverse-proxy tunnel. After creating the project, run `replayqa proxy --project <project_id>` on a machine that can reach target_url. The old setup instructions remain available from GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/reverse-proxy as `instructions`.

enabled_polish_passes.description: Which polish passes run against the project's test runs. Replaces the default set entirely, so include every pass you want enabled. Prefer add_polish_passes / remove_polish_passes unless you really mean to pin the whole set — a hardcoded copy of the defaults goes stale when the defaults change. Unknown pass names are rejected with a 400.

add_polish_passes.description: Polish passes to enable ON TOP of the default set (or on top of enabled_polish_passes when that is sent too). Use this to turn on a pass that is off by default — e.g. ["seo"] runs the defaults plus the SEO pass — without restating the defaults. Unknown pass names are rejected with a 400.

remove_polish_passes.description: Polish passes to disable from the default set (or from enabled_polish_passes when that is sent too). Naming a pass in both add_polish_passes and remove_polish_passes is rejected with a 400.

time_limit_minutes.description: Wall-clock limit in minutes for each new test run, including queueing, retries and recording analysis. Omit or send null for no limit. Each run snapshots its deadline when created; changing this setting affects future runs only. When a deadline expires, the project is paused, all remaining project work is cancelled and eligible unfinished work is refunded. Finished results are preserved. Running containers are stopped by the next deadline sweep (every minute in production; previews use the five-minute reap sweep).

budget.description: Credit budget cap for this project — the maximum number of credits QA may spend on it. QA pauses once this cap is reached (raise it later to resume). Rough guide: ~10 = smoke test, 20–50 = thorough, 50+ = broad coverage. Off by default: omit it to leave the project with no per-project cap (QA is bounded only by your account balance).

security_ownership_exempt.description: Waive the security pass's ownership check for this project. Active security probing normally refuses to send any request until the target origin echoes a nonce placed at /.well-known/replay-qa-security-nonce, proving you control it; set this when the target is an app you deploy and that check is not workable. RESTRICTED: a request that sets this field from an account without the entitlement is rejected with a 403 (ask an admin to grant it). The waiver skips only the nonce fetch — a cloned/emulated target is still never probed, and only origins on the target site's own registrable domain are ever contacted.

200.description: Created project with exploration_id (null when start_exploration is false) and url (link to the project dashboard). When use_reverse_proxy is true the response also includes reverse_proxy_setup_url — poll it for the tunnel setup instructions.

post.summary: Enable reverse proxy and ensure the matching project environment
post.description: Idempotently creates or updates the Local environment for an interactive client or the Preview environment for CI, enables reverse proxy, and returns tunnel status.

target_url.description: Local or private-network app URL reachable from the frpc client, for example http://localhost:3000.

connection_purpose.description: Interactive clients create Local; CI clients create Preview and retain their PR through run provenance.

200.description: Reverse-proxy status plus the ensured Local or Preview environment.

400.description: The first reverse-proxy setup requires a valid target_url.

get.summary: Get reverse-proxy tunnel status and the setup instructions to connect it
get.description:
For reverse-proxy projects. Legacy projects without a named Local environment get one automatically
from their existing target URL. Existing public projects should first POST a local target URL here.
Returns the tunnel status plus a self-contained,
copy-paste runbook (the `instructions` field) that an agent runs on a machine that can reach target_url:
install frpc, build a small allowlist-restricted local forward proxy, write the config, and run — all
outbound-only, no inbound ports.

The tunnel is provisioned lazily on the first call, so `instructions` is null for the first minute or two
while it spins up — keep polling until it is non-null. Once frpc connects, `ready` flips to true, the
project gate opens, and QA starts automatically (no further action). Restrict the forward proxy to the
app's host plus any backend/auth/CDN hosts it calls during testing.

200.description: Reverse-proxy status. Fields: enabled, state (provisioning|active|error|ended|unconfigured), ready (true once frpc is connected and replayqa proxy reports a healthy local data path), frpc_connected, client_health, reverse_proxy_status (pending|ready), cli_command, instructions (advanced fallback setup runbook, or null while provisioning), tunnel (connection details, or null).

enabled_polish_passes.description: Which polish passes run against the project's test runs. Replaces the enabled set entirely, so include every pass you want enabled; pass [] to disable all. Unknown pass names are rejected with a 400.

add_polish_passes.description: Polish passes to enable, applied to the project's CURRENT set (or to enabled_polish_passes when that is sent too). Lets you turn one pass on without reading the current set first. Unknown pass names are rejected with a 400.

remove_polish_passes.description: Polish passes to disable, applied to the project's CURRENT set (or to enabled_polish_passes when that is sent too). Naming a pass in both add_polish_passes and remove_polish_passes is rejected with a 400. One of enabled_polish_passes, add_polish_passes, remove_polish_passes, security_ownership_exempt, github, status, target_url, or time_limit_minutes is required.

RESTRICTED: a request that sets this field from an account without the entitlement is rejected with a 403 (ask an admin to grant it). The waiver skips only the nonce fetch — a cloned/emulated target is still never probed, and only origins on the target site's own registrable domain are ever contacted.

target_url_pattern.description: Full-URL pattern the preview URL must match; * matches anything, case-insensitive.

completion_check_name.description: Check-run name of the job that finishes the preview deploy; its success triggers scraping the URL from PR comments.

workflow_path.description: Workflow file that deploys the preview. Informational.

accessTokenSet.description: Whether a personal access token is stored. Ignored on write.

target_url.description: Replace the project default app URL for future QA runs. Must be a nonempty HTTP(S) URL. Environment and run overrides still take precedence.

time_limit_minutes.description: Wall-clock limit in minutes for each new test run, including queueing, retries and recording analysis. Omit or send null for no limit. Each run snapshots its deadline when created; changing this setting affects future runs only. When a deadline expires, the project is paused, all remaining project work is cancelled and eligible unfinished work is refunded. Finished results are preserved. Running containers are stopped by the next deadline sweep (every minute in production; previews use the five-minute reap sweep).

status.description: Pause or resume all QA work for the project. Pausing prevents queued work from starting; resuming starts processing the existing queue again.

200.description: Updated project

post.summary: Cancel an active test run without deleting its history
post.description: Stops active and queued work belonging to this test-run session while preserving its runs, recordings, explorations, and findings. The test_run_id is the session id returned by the project test-runs collection.

200.description: Cancellation result and preserved journey-run/exploration counts.

404.description: Test run not found in this project.

patch.summary: Reorder, expedite, or skip pending journey test runs
patch.description: Edits journey work that is still queued. Use move with neighbouring task ids to place one item precisely, run-next to move selected items to the front of their priority class, or skip to cancel selected pending runs without deleting their history. Queue task ids are returned with queued journeys and test runs.

200.description: The moved task or affected task ids.

409.description: The queue changed before the edit could be applied.

get.summary: Get project summary with counts of explorations, journeys, test runs, and bugs

200.description: Project status summary

get.summary: Get a project's key timing milestones as absolute, comparable timestamps
get.description:
Returns the project's timing milestones on a single server clock, so a consumer can measure
how long QA took to start producing activity and to finish without draining event streams.

Fields:
- `created_at` — when the project was created (ISO 8601 UTC).
- `started_at` — when work actually began (earliest task start), or null if none has started yet.
- `first_event_at` — server-side arrival time of the earliest rrweb event across ALL of the
  project's recordings (explorations + test runs); null if no events yet.
- `finished_at` — when the project last went idle; null while QA is still running.
- `time_to_first_event_ms` / `time_to_complete_ms` — deltas measured from `created_at`
  (null when the corresponding timestamp is null).

200.description: Project timing milestones

get.summary: List Playwright test analyses and project processing counts

200.description: Newest-first analyses with submitted test context and reports, plus total, processing, completed and failed counts.

post.summary: Analyze an uploaded Replay recording of a failed Playwright attempt
post.description: Queues a recording-only investigation in an active project. Repeated submissions for the same CI run, test, retry and recording reuse the analysis. Costs one task credit. Does not explore the live target or automatically file findings as bugs.

202.description: Analysis ID and relative status_url; poll for the report.

get.summary: Read failure-analysis progress and its report

200.description: status, input recording_id, driver_recording_id, and report (null until available). Report contains classification, explanation, root_cause, evidence, next_step, and limitations.

404.description: Analysis not found in this project

get.summary: Stream the rrweb recording and narration events used by the replay player
get.description:
Returns the ordered player event rows for one task, test run, exploration, or Replay recording.
The stream contains rrweb DOM events plus the thought, note, error, and system events shown as
replay subtitles. It excludes injected diagnostic streams such as network-exchange and layout-geometry.

## Rendering the rrweb stream

1. Fetch pages in order. When `next_cursor` is non-null, make the same request again with its
   `after_task_id` and `after_seq`; stop when `next_cursor` is null.
2. Reassemble `rrweb-chunk` rows before rendering. Each chunk payload is
   `{ chunk_id, index, total, data }`. Group by `chunk_id`, order all `total` pieces by `index`,
   concatenate `data`, and `JSON.parse` the result. Treat the completed row as `event_type: "rrweb"`.
   Keep the incomplete-chunk map across page requests because one event can span pages.
3. Select rows whose `event_type` is `rrweb`, in their returned order, and pass their `payload` values
   to rrweb. The array must include rrweb Meta and FullSnapshot events before it can render:

```js
import { Replayer } from 'rrweb'
import 'rrweb/dist/style.css'

const events = joinedRows.filter(row => row.event_type === 'rrweb').map(row => row.payload)
const replayer = new Replayer(events, { root: document.querySelector("#replay") })
replayer.play()
```

For a recording that is still running, retain the Replayer and call `replayer.addEvent(row.payload)` for
new rrweb rows instead of rebuilding it. Sort by `payload.timestamp` only if events were accumulated from
multiple live polls that may have arrived out of timestamp order.

## Rendering narration

`thought`, `note`, `error`, and `system` rows are subtitles, not rrweb events. Use `client_ts` as the
subtitle timestamp, falling back to `Date.parse(created_at)` when it is null. Their text is normally in
`payload.text` or `payload.message`; `note` payloads with `kind: "step"` also carry the action and step index.

A genuinely different defect needs its own evidence and report. wontfix: the issue is acknowledged and will recur, but new bugs should not be filed for it; match recurring findings to this report. get.summary: List test journeys (user flows) defined for a project

200.description: List of journeys

post.description:
Creates an unstepped journey — one with no scripted steps. An AI agent reads the
journey name, description, and instructions, then drives the app with Playwright to
carry out the flow, recording the session and filing any bugs it finds.

If the project is active, the journey is scheduled to run immediately. Use `target_url`
to point this journey at a URL different from the project's base URL (e.g. a deep link
or a different environment) — that URL is where the recording is created. Set `polish`
to also run the project's enabled polish passes against the resulting recording.

name.description: Short name for the journey (the flow under test).

description.description: What the agent should do — the scenario to carry out in the app.

instructions.description: Optional extra guidance / post-run checks for the agent.

target_url.description: Optional URL to record this journey against, overriding the project's base URL. When omitted, the project's URL is used.

polish.description: When true, the project's enabled polish passes also run against this journey's recording.

get.summary: Get a journey with its versions and the bugs associated with it
get.description: Returns the journey (including its target_url override, if any, and version history) plus `bugs`: every bug filed by this journey's test runs.

200.description: Journey detail with associated bugs

get.summary: Get an exploration with the journeys it discovered and the bugs associated with it
get.description: Returns the exploration plus `journeys` (the journeys it created/updated) and `bugs` (polish-pass findings against the exploration's own recording). Each discovered journey's own bugs are available via GET /journeys/{journey_id}.

200.description: Exploration detail with discovered journeys and associated bugs

post.summary: Record a new app version and trigger a version-added task
post.description:
Records a new deployed version of the app (git SHA, branch, timestamp, deployed URL,
optional change description). Adding a version kicks off a version-added task that reviews
the change and keeps the project's journeys in sync — it adds new journeys, and for
main-branch versions may update/delete existing ones, then triggers test runs for the
new/changed journeys. Requires the project to have a GitHub link and main branch configured
in its settings.

git_sha.description: Git commit SHA for this version.

branch_name.description: Git branch name the version was deployed from.

deployed_url.description: URL where this version is deployed (defaults to the project URL).

change_description.description: Human-readable summary of what changed in this version.

201.description: Created version (its version-added task is queued).
